chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sheep and the cow, that sometimes they yield milk without the ram striking/mating with them, and the hen, that sometimes she lays eggs without the rooster mounting her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'All of this is permissible and pure for you. Everything whose meat is edible, all that comes from it—whether milk, or eggs, or rennet—is permissible and pure. And sometimes this occurs after the ram has mated with her, yet it is delayed; and all of this is permissible.'
ai.seo_question: Is milk and eggs from cows and chickens permissible if they are produced without mating?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses this narration to clarify that the primary criterion for the permissibility of animal by-products is the inherent halal status of the animal itself, rather than the specific mechanism of production. This ruling addresses practical concerns regarding spontaneous lactation or ovulation, affirming that such natural occurrences do not introduce impurity (najāsah) or impermissibility, thereby simplifying dietary laws for the community.
